integration_decisions: Preserved the concurrent scheduler, injectable native executor, all six controller tests, native effect/follow/source regressions and non-Unix synchronous fallback.
Preserved sixteen pending native requests, thirty-second output delivery allowance (now absolute from enqueue) and actual completed-native-response delivery through cancellation.
The earlier local alternative used eight queued requests and suppressed cancelled replies; it was not published over the concurrent implementation.

A complete tools/list reply with a maximum escaped request ID exceeded the former control allowance by 140 bytes. The aggregate control allowance is now 256 KiB with a focused full-catalog regression.
Preserved the concurrent 17cc7d1 native refinement: follow parks check cancellation in at most 25 ms slices, and session cancellation keeps its native cancelled outcome before clock admission.

Ported lifecycle ownership onto the newer Outbox and shared stdio owners; preserved permanent session IDs, native reply reservation, full allocation accounting, final-newline delivery, finite write attempts and pending-flush identity ownership.

semantics.identity: Decoded strings and signed integer IDs are distinct; -0 and 0 share numeric identity. Up to 4096 valid identities remain reserved for the entire live session, including refusals and completed deliveries. Reuse receives id:null/-32600; the next new identity at the ceiling receives -32000 and stops intake while accepted work drains.
semantics.output: One native result slot and maximum escaped result bytes are held before starting work. Control replies cannot spend that reservation. Full owned allocations remain charged through newline; identity and frame counts remain reserved through pending flush. Every response keeps its enqueue time through its final newline and pending flush. Thirty seconds is an absolute delivery allowance; partial progress and later metadata do not renew it. Every write and flush admission checks the oldest outstanding delivery.
semantics.cancellation: Queued work never executes; running work remains owned until its exact closure and coordinator join. Available native results remain authoritative and are returned even if cancellation raced completion. Cancellation cannot undo an effect.
semantics.EOF: Seal intake and drain accepted native commands and replies.
semantics.failure: Framing/I/O/output pressure failure discards unstarted work and pending output, requests active cancellation and joins before returning. Panic, indeterminate work, failed region admission or unconfirmed closure quarantine the connection before successors execute. Actual completed native results are retained even if region close fails.
semantics.stdio: Both inherited descriptors share one restoration lease; original flags are sampled before either changes and restored only after both owners retire. Non-Unix retains the existing synchronous implementation.
semantics.deadline: One 60-second deadline starts at native queue admission and is inherited by a distinct child region. Queue/output pressure cannot renew it. Expired queued work never executes. Active expiry requests cooperative cancellation, joins the worker and closes its region; admitted effects and filesystem calls are not preempted.
